label.description: The panel's accessible name. Set, the panel becomes a named role="group"; empty, it carries no role at all. A PANEL HOLDING CONTROLS MUST SET IT: role="group" is in neither the accessibility lint's content-named roles nor its labelled roles, so an unnamed one is invisible to every gate, and a non-modal group of form controls with no role and no name announces no boundary on entry. A panel holding only a jx-menu leaves it empty, because the menu carries its own name.

arrow.description: Draw a pointer at the panel's block-start edge. Decorative and aria-hidden; off by default, because a panel placed by measured coordinates cannot promise the arrow lands on its anchor. THE PANEL ITSELF NEVER SCROLLS: the scroll box is [part="content"], because a scroll container clips whatever hangs outside its padding box and the arrow hangs 5px above it; with overflow on the host the arrow paints nothing at all.

matchWidth.description: Make the panel at least as wide as the element it was opened from, the way a select's list matches its trigger. The width is re-measured on each toggle and never continuously, from whatever the toggle names as its source: a raw <button popovertarget>, a kit button forwarding popovertarget, and openAt(panel, trigger) all measure the trigger.

placement.description: Where the panel sits relative to the element it was opened from, as a CSS position-area value: block-end span-inline-end (below, its inline-start edge on the trigger's) by default; block-end span-inline-start for a panel that hangs from a trigger's trailing edge; block-start for one that opens above. It applies only while the panel is ANCHORED, which is whenever it was shown from a source, and only on an engine with CSS anchor positioning: the trigger becomes the popover's implicit anchor the moment it is passed to showPopover({ source }) or names the panel with popovertarget, so no anchor-name is ever written on a consumer's element (specs/ui.md 2, 6). Everywhere else the panel stands at x and y. The value is passed to the property as written and is not validated here, because the platform's own grammar is the contract and a value it refuses computes to none, which is the coordinate placement again.

x.description: Where the panel's inline-start edge sits, in viewport pixels, whenever the panel is NOT anchored: shown with no source, given a floor, or on an engine without CSS anchor positioning. A panel shown from a source is placed by the platform against that source (see placement) and ignores x and y, though an opener may still write them, because they are exactly the fallback the anchored rule stands on.

y.description: Where the panel's block-start edge sits, in viewport pixels, under the same condition as x. The gap between that edge and the anchor is the --jx-popover-offset token, not a prop: a numeric prop with a non-zero default cannot express "unset", because removing its attribute coerces through the current value's type and writes 0. Anchored, the same margin is the gap below the trigger.

floor.description: The lowest edge the panel may reach, in viewport pixels; 0 means the viewport's bottom. A panel opened from a rail that abuts a status bar sets it to the rail's bottom, so a tall panel never runs down over the bar.

open.description: Whether the panel is showing. THIS IS NOT A DOOR: writing el.open = true shows nothing. It follows the platform's toggle event; write it through showPopover() and hidePopover(), or through the openAt() and close() helpers in the behaviours module, not directly.

settling.description: Whether a discrete open or close transition is still running. Mirrored as data-jx-settling, so a host can wait for the panel to come to rest before measuring it.

anchorWidth.description: The measured border-box width of the element the panel was opened from, in pixels. Written by the behaviour under matchWidth and read by the panel's own min-width; 0 when nothing has been measured.

anchored.description: Whether the panel is showing from a source the platform knows, and therefore positioned by anchor rather than by x and y. Written by the behaviour on beforetoggle, before the panel is laid out, so the first frame is already in the right place; cleared when it closes. Mirrored as data-anchored, which the anchored rule keys on. Not an attribute, because it is the platform's fact and never a consumer's to set. A panel given a floor is never anchored: a floor is a limit the platform's fallbacks cannot express, so it keeps the coordinate placement the clamp honours.

onBeforeToggle.description: Decides anchored before the panel is laid out: an opening toggle whose source the platform names, on a panel with no floor, is anchored; everything else is not. On beforetoggle rather than toggle because toggle is queued after the show and a panel that learned it was anchored one frame late would paint once at its coordinates and then jump.

onToggle.description: Mirrors the platform's toggle event into open, raises settling for the transition, measures the anchor under matchWidth, and clamps a freshly shown panel into the viewport when it is not anchored; an anchored panel is placed and flipped by the platform and is left alone.

onTransitionEnd.description: Clears settling when the panel's own transition finishes. A transition on a child is not the panel coming to rest, so only an event whose target is the host counts.

onMount.description: Announces that the element has rendered and carries its popover attribute, so a host may show it. A panel is always an auto popover: light dismiss, Escape and focus restoration are the platform's.

style.transition: opacity var(--jx-dur-1) var(--jx-ease-out), display var(--jx-dur-1) allow-discrete, overlay var(--jx-dur-1) allow-discrete

@supports (position-area: block-end).$description: The anchored placement, and the whole of what CSS anchor positioning gives a panel: the platform puts it against its IMPLICIT anchor — the element it was shown from — follows that element through scroll and resize, and flips it to the other side when the first placement would overflow, none of which a measured coordinate can do without a listener per cause. No anchor-name is involved: a popover's invoker is its implicit anchor by the platform's own rule, which is what makes this reachable under ui.md 2 (an element writes no style on a consumer's trigger). The insets are released so x and y stop mattering, and matchWidth becomes anchor-size, which follows the trigger as it resizes where the measured width could not. Outside this block, and on a panel shown from nothing or with a floor, the coordinate placement above is the answer, unchanged.
